medical_conditions.name: Minor Cut / Wound
first_aid: Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water before touching the wound.
Apply gentle direct pressure with a clean cloth or bandage until bleeding stops.
Clean the wound under running tap water; clean surrounding skin with mild soap.
Apply a thin layer of over-the-counter antiseptic ointment if available.
Cover the wound with a sterile adhesive bandage or sterile dressing.
do_not: Do NOT blow on the open wound.
Do NOT use harsh chemicals like hydrogen peroxide or full-strength alcohol directly inside the open wound.
Do NOT remove embedded deep foreign objects yourself.
warning_signs: Bleeding does not stop after 10 minutes of direct pressure
Wound is deep, gaping, or caused by rusty metal or animal bite
Pus, increasing redness, swelling, or throbbing pain develops later

medicine_information.name: Antiseptic Cream / Ointment (Betadine / Neosporin)
medicine_information.purpose: Helps prevent bacterial skin infection on minor cuts
medicine_information.warning: For external skin use only. Discontinue if rash or irritation occurs.

medical_conditions.name: Thermal Burn (Minor)
first_aid: Immediately cool the burn under cool running tap water for 10-15 minutes.
Remove rings or tight items from the burned area before swelling starts.
Apply aloe vera gel or burn ointment after cooling.
Cover loosely with a clean, sterile non-stick bandage.
do_not: Do NOT apply ice, ice water, butter, oil, or toothpastes to the burn.
Do NOT break or pop blisters.
Do NOT use fluffy cotton balls that can stick to the burn.
warning_signs: Burn covers face, hands, groin, or major joint
Burn area appears charred, black, or white
Signs of severe infection or fever develop

medicine_information.name: Aloe Vera Gel / Silver Sulfadiazine (Burnol)
medicine_information.purpose: Soothes skin and provides moisture to minor 1st degree burns
medicine_information.warning: External application only. Seek medical help for large or deep burns.

medical_conditions.name: Viral Fever
first_aid: Rest adequately in a comfortable, well-ventilated room.
Drink plenty of fluids (water, clear broths, oral rehydration solution).
Use a cool damp cloth on forehead for comfort if temperature is high.
Wear light, breathable clothing.
do_not: Do NOT take antibiotics without explicit prescription from a registered physician.
Do NOT bundle up in heavy blankets if shivering with high fever.
Do NOT give aspirin to children or teenagers.
warning_signs: Fever exceeds 103°F (39.4°C) or lasts more than 3 days
Severe headache, neck stiffness, or confusion
Difficulty breathing or persistent chest discomfort

medicine_information.name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
medicine_information.purpose: Temporary relief of mild-to-moderate fever and body pain
medicine_information.warning: Do not exceed maximum daily limit. Consult doctor before taking if liver conditions exist.

medical_conditions.name: Tension Headache / Migraine
first_aid: Rest in a quiet, dark, and cool room.
Place a cold compress or ice pack wrapped in a towel on your forehead or back of neck.
Stay hydrated by drinking small sips of water.
Practice slow deep breathing to relax tension.
do_not: Do NOT stare at bright mobile/computer screens.
Do NOT consume excessive caffeine or alcohol.
warning_signs: Sudden, extremely severe 'thunderclap' headache
Headache accompanied by fever, stiff neck, or confusion
Headache following a head injury

medicine_information.name: Paracetamol / Ibuprofen
medicine_information.purpose: Symptomatic relief of mild to moderate headache pain
medicine_information.warning: Take strictly as instructed. Seek medical consultation for frequent headaches.

medical_conditions.name: Dehydration / Heat Exhaustion
first_aid: Move to a cool, shaded, or air-conditioned area immediately.
Sip oral rehydration solution (ORS), electrolyte water, or cool fluids slowly.
Loosen tight clothing and remove extra layers.
Apply cool wet towels to neck, armpits, and forehead.
do_not: Do NOT gulp down large quantities of fluids rapidly.
Do NOT drink caffeinated, sugary, or alcoholic beverages.
Do NOT ignore dizziness or muscle cramps in hot weather.
warning_signs: Confusion, slurred speech, or delirium (Heat Stroke emergency)
Inability to keep fluids down / persistent vomiting
No urination for over 8 hours

medicine_information.name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS)
medicine_information.purpose: Restores lost fluids and essential electrolytes
medicine_information.warning: Mix strictly in clean drinking water according to packet instructions.

medical_conditions.name: Gastroenteritis / Food Poisoning
first_aid: Let your stomach settle for a couple of hours after vomiting.
Sip small amounts of ORS, clear broths, or electrolyte solutions.
Gradually reintroduce bland foods (BRAT diet: Banana, Rice, Applesauce, Toast).
Get plenty of physical rest.
do_not: Do NOT eat greasy, spicy, or fried foods.
Do NOT take anti-diarrheal medications without consulting a physician if blood is present in stool.
warning_signs: Inability to keep any liquids down for more than 12-24 hours
Blood in vomit or stool
High fever above 102°F or signs of severe dehydration

medicine_information.name: Oral Rehydration Solutions (ORS)
medicine_information.warning: Crucial for preventing dehydration. Seek medical evaluation for persistent vomiting.

medical_conditions.name: Joint Sprain / Ligament Injury
first_aid: Follow R.I.C.E protocol: Rest, Ice, Compress, Elevate.
Ice: Apply ice pack wrapped in a towel for 15-20 minutes every 2-3 hours.
Compress: Lightly wrap joint with an elastic bandage.
Elevate: Prop up the injured limb above heart level when resting.
do_not: Do NOT apply direct heat or hot packs in the first 48 hours.
Do NOT attempt to walk on a severely injured leg or ankle if pain is severe.
warning_signs: Inability to bear any weight on the limb
Visible deformity or bone protrusion
Numbness, tingling, or severe pale coldness in toes/fingers

medicine_information.name: Diclofenac Gel (Volini) / Ibuprofen
medicine_information.purpose: Helps reduce joint inflammation and localized pain
medicine_information.warning: Apply topically on intact skin. Avoid open wounds.

medical_conditions.name: Minor Allergic Reaction
first_aid: Identify and remove the allergen if known (dust, pollen, pet dander).
Wash affected skin area with mild soap and cool water.
Apply cool compresses to itchy skin.
Take over-the-counter antihistamine as recommended by a pharmacist or doctor.
do_not: Do NOT scratch itchy skin heavily to prevent secondary infection.
Do NOT ignore spreading throat tightness or facial swelling.
warning_signs: Swelling of lips, tongue, or throat
Difficulty breathing, wheezing, or tightness in chest
Dizziness, confusion, or rapid drop in blood pressure

medicine_information.name: Cetirizine / Loratadine
medicine_information.purpose: Antihistamine for relief of allergic itching, sneezing, and hives
medicine_information.warning: May cause mild drowsiness. Use as directed.

medical_conditions.name: Nosebleed (Epistaxis)
first_aid: Sit upright and lean slightly forward (do NOT lean back).
Pinch the soft lower part of your nose firmly between thumb and index finger.
Hold pinch continuously for 10-15 minutes without releasing.
Breathe through your mouth while pinching.
Apply a cold ice pack to the bridge of the nose.
do_not: Do NOT tilt your head back; blood may flow down the throat and cause choking or vomiting.
Do NOT blow your nose or pick your nose for several hours after bleeding stops.
warning_signs: Bleeding continues for more than 20 minutes of continuous pressure
Bleeding is extremely heavy or accompanied by dizziness/fainting
Nosebleed occurs after a violent head blow

medicine_information.name: Saline Nasal Drops
medicine_information.purpose: Moisturizes nasal passages to prevent dryness and nosebleeds

medical_conditions.name: Insect Bite / Sting
first_aid: Remove sting sac if visible by scraping gently with a card edge.
Wash the area thoroughly with soap and water.
Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth for 10 minutes to reduce swelling.
Apply calamine lotion or aloe gel to soothe itching.
do_not: Do NOT scratch the sting area.
Do NOT squeeze the stinger.
warning_signs: Swelling spreads to lips, throat, or mouth
Difficulty breathing or generalized hives across whole body
Signs of anaphylactic shock

medicine_information.name: Calamine Lotion / Hydrocortisone Cream
medicine_information.purpose: Relieves localized itching and inflammation from insect stings

first_aid_guides.title: Fracture & Bone Injury
first_aid_guides.what_happened: A bone is cracked or broken due to trauma, fall, or high impact.
immediate_first_aid: Keep the injured area completely still and immobilized.
Do NOT attempt to push back a protruding bone or realign the limb.
Apply an ice pack wrapped in a cloth to reduce swelling without pressing hard.
If trained, apply a temporary splint above and below the fracture site.
do_list: Keep the victim calm and warm.
Support the injured limb in the position found.
Call emergency medical services immediately.
dont_list: Do NOT move the person if spinal or neck injury is suspected.
Do NOT test the limb by trying to walk or bend it.
Do NOT give food or drink in case emergency surgery is needed.
when_to_seek_help: Bone is visible through torn skin (open fracture)
Limb is numb, pale, or blue at extremities
Severe unbearable pain or inability to move

first_aid_guides.title: Thermal & Chemical Burns
first_aid_guides.what_happened: Skin damage caused by heat, fire, hot liquid, steam, or corrosive chemical contact.
immediate_first_aid: Cool burn under cool running tap water for 10-20 minutes.
For chemical burns, flush continuously with water for at least 20 minutes.
Remove jewelry or constricting items before swelling occurs.
Cover loosely with a clean, sterile non-stick bandage.
do_list: FLUSH continuously with water.
Protect burned area from dirt and contamination.
Seek urgent medical advice for major burns.
dont_list: Do NOT apply ice, butter, grease, toothpaste, or oil.
Do NOT peel off clothing stuck to burned skin.
when_to_seek_help: Burn is larger than 3 inches in diameter
Burn is on face, hands, feet, groin, or major joint
Burn is caused by chemicals or electrical source

first_aid_guides.title: Severe External Bleeding
first_aid_guides.what_happened: Deep cut or vascular laceration resulting in rapid blood loss.
immediate_first_aid: Apply direct, firm pressure on wound with a sterile gauze or clean cloth.
Maintain pressure continuously without lifting the cloth to check.
If blood soaks through, add another cloth on top.
Elevate wound above heart level if safe.
Call emergency services immediately.
do_list: Use sterile gloves or clean barrier if available.
Keep victim lying down and quiet.
Monitor breathing and consciousness.
dont_list: Do NOT remove original soaked cloth bandage.
Do NOT apply tourniquet unless trained and direct pressure fails.
when_to_seek_help: Bleeding does not stop after 10 minutes of direct pressure
Victim feels faint, dizzy, or shows signs of shock

first_aid_guides.title: Choking & Airway Obstruction
first_aid_guides.what_happened: Food or foreign object blocks the trachea, preventing airflow.
immediate_first_aid: If person CANNOT cough, speak, or breathe:
Give 5 sharp back blows between shoulder blades with heel of hand.
Give 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver): Stand behind, wrap arms around waist, place fist above navel, thrust upward and inward.
Repeat cycle until object is dislodged or person becomes unconscious.
Call emergency services immediately.
do_list: Act immediately; choking can cause brain damage within minutes.
Begin CPR compressions if person collapses.
dont_list: Do NOT perform abdominal thrusts on infants under 1 year (use chest thrusts).
Do NOT slap back while person is standing upright without leaning forward.
when_to_seek_help: Choking obstruction is not dislodged immediately
Person becomes unresponsive or turns blue

first_aid_guides.title: Heat Stroke & Exhaustion
first_aid_guides.what_happened: Overheating of the body due to high ambient temperatures and dehydration.
immediate_first_aid: Move person to a cool, shaded or air-conditioned room.
Remove excess or tight clothing.
Cool person rapidly: apply ice packs to armpits, groin, and neck, or spray with cool water.
Give small sips of cool water or electrolyte drink if conscious.
do_list: Fan the person while dampening skin.
Monitor body temperature.
Call emergency services if confusion or high fever is present.
dont_list: Do NOT give fluids if person is confused or vomiting.
Do NOT give aspirin or paracetamol for heat stroke.
when_to_seek_help: Confusion, agitation, slurred speech, or seizures occur

first_aid_guides.title: Anaphylactic Shock
first_aid_guides.what_happened: Severe life-threatening allergic reaction to food, venom, or medicine.
immediate_first_aid: Call emergency services immediately.
If person has a prescribed epinephrine auto-injector (EpiPen), assist them in using it on outer mid-thigh.
Have person lie flat on back with feet elevated.
If breathing is difficult, allow them to sit up.
do_list: Stay with person continuously.
Be prepared to give second dose of epinephrine after 5-15 minutes if symptoms persist.
dont_list: Do NOT place pillow under head if breathing is difficult.
Do NOT delay calling emergency services even if EpiPen was given.
when_to_seek_help: Swelling of lips/throat, wheezing, or loss of consciousness

first_aid_guides.title: Snake Bite & Animal Bite
first_aid_guides.what_happened: Puncture wound or envenomation from snake, dog, or wild animal.
immediate_first_aid: Keep victim calm and still to slow venom spread.
Remove tight clothing, rings, or watch near the bite area.
Clean wound gently with soap and water.
Immobilize the bitten limb at or slightly below heart level.
Transport victim to nearest hospital emergency room immediately.
do_list: Note the snake's appearance (color, pattern) from a safe distance.
Seek anti-venom medical treatment urgently.
dont_list: Do NOT cut into the bite wound or suck out venom.
Do NOT apply tourniquet or ice packs to snake bite.
when_to_seek_help: All snake bites require immediate hospital emergency evaluation!

first_aid_guides.title: High Fever & Convulsions
first_aid_guides.what_happened: Spike in body temperature causing febrile seizure or distress.
immediate_first_aid: Place person on their side in a recovery position.
Clear area around them to prevent injury.
Apply cool sponge bath on forehead and neck.
Administer oral rehydration fluids when fully conscious.
do_list: Keep track of time seizure lasts.
Consult a pediatrician/doctor for fever evaluation.
dont_list: Do NOT restrain person during seizure.
Do NOT put anything into their mouth.
when_to_seek_help: Fever exceeds 103°F or is accompanied by stiff neck

medicines.name: Paracetamol (Crocin / Dolo 650 / Calpol)
common_uses: Temporary relief of mild to moderate fever
Headache, toothache, and body pain relief
Minor muscular aches and flu discomfort
important_warnings: Do not exceed 4000 mg (4 grams) total daily dose for adults.
Overdose can cause severe liver damage.
Avoid alcohol consumption while taking paracetamol.
contraindications: Severe liver impairment or acute hepatitis
medicines.disclaimer: Consult a qualified doctor or pharmacist before taking any medication.

medicines.name: Ibuprofen (Advil / Combiflam)
common_uses: Reduction of swelling and localized inflammation
Joint pain, ligament sprains, and backache
Toothache and menstrual cramps
important_warnings: Take with food or milk to minimize stomach irritation.
Long-term use increases risk of stomach ulcers and GI bleeding.
contraindications: Active stomach ulcers or history of GI bleeding
Severe kidney disease or severe heart failure
medicines.disclaimer: Consult a qualified doctor or pharmacist before taking any medication.

medicines.name: Oral Rehydration Salts (ORS / Electral)
common_uses: Dehydration caused by diarrhea, vomiting, or stomach flu
Heat exhaustion, intense sun exposure, and excessive sweating
Strenuous physical effort or sports recovery
important_warnings: Dissolve packet contents strictly in the exact volume of clean drinking water specified on label.
Do not boil the solution after mixing.
contraindications: Intestinal obstruction or severe kidney dysfunction (requires medical monitoring)
medicines.disclaimer: Consult a doctor if dehydration symptoms worsen or persistent vomiting prevents fluid retention.

medicines.name: Cetirizine (Cetzine / Okacet)
common_uses: Relief of allergic rhinitis (sneezing, runny nose, watery eyes)
Hives (urticaria) and skin itching
Insect sting and mosquito bite skin reactions
important_warnings: May cause mild drowsiness in some individuals.
Avoid operating heavy machinery or driving if affected.
medicines.disclaimer: Consult a doctor or pharmacist for proper dosage guidance.

medicines.name: Antacid Gel / Tablets (Gelusil / Digene / Eno)
common_uses: Quick relief of heartburn and acid indigestion
Upset stomach due to hyperacidity or overeating
Sour stomach and gas bloat discomfort
important_warnings: May alter absorption of other medications; take 2 hours apart from other drugs.
Excessive use may cause bowel changes (diarrhea or constipation).
medicines.disclaimer: Do not use continuously for more than 14 days without consulting a medical practitioner.

medicines.name: Povidone-Iodine (Betadine Ointment / Liquid)
common_uses: Disinfecting minor cuts, scrapes, and superficial wounds
Preventing bacterial infection in skin lacerations and minor burns
Pre-dressing wound cleaning
important_warnings: For external skin application only.
Avoid contact with eyes. Discontinue if skin irritation or rash occurs.
medicines.disclaimer: External application only. Seek medical attention for deep or heavily bleeding wounds.

medicines.name: Neosporin / Triple Antibiotic Ointment
common_uses: First-aid protection against infection in minor cuts, scrapes, and burns
Keeping minor wound beds clean and moist under dressing
important_warnings: For external topical skin use only.
Do not apply over large body areas or deep puncture wounds.
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to neomycin, polymyxin, or bacitracin
medicines.disclaimer: Consult a doctor if skin condition persists or worsens after 7 days.

medicines.name: Diclofenac Gel (Volini / Omnigel / Moov)
common_uses: Relief of muscle strain, joint pain, and ankle sprains
Localized backache, neck pain, and muscular stiffness
Sports injury recovery
important_warnings: Apply topically on intact, unbroken skin only.
Wash hands thoroughly after applying. Do not apply near eyes or open wounds.
contraindications: Open wounds, infected skin, or severe eczema
medicines.disclaimer: Topical pain relief gel for temporary muscular discomfort.

medicines.name: Calamine Lotion
common_uses: Relief of itching from insect bites and bee stings
Soothes sunburn, mild rash, and chickenpox itching
Drying weeping skin irritations
important_warnings: For external skin application only. Shake well before use.
Avoid contact with eyes, mouth, and mucous membranes.
contraindications: Open deep wounds or severe third-degree burns
medicines.disclaimer: Consult a healthcare provider if rash worsens or persists beyond 7 days.

medicines.name: Silver Sulfadiazine Cream (Burnol)
common_uses: Soothing minor 1st and 2nd degree thermal burns
Preventing infection in minor skin scalds and heat burns
important_warnings: For topical burn application only.
Clean burn area under cool water before applying a thin layer.
contraindications: Pregnant women near term or infants under 2 months
medicines.disclaimer: Seek urgent hospital emergency care for major or deep burns.

medicines.name: Aloe Vera Gel
common_uses: Cooling minor sun burns and thermal skin heat
Soothing dry, irritated, or itchy skin
Post-insect sting skin hydration
important_warnings: For external topical use.
Perform a patch test if sensitive skin.
medicines.disclaimer: Natural soothing agent for minor skin discomfort.

medicines.name: Dextromethorphan Cough Syrup (Benadryl DR / Ascoril D)
common_uses: Relief of dry, tickly, non-productive cough
Throat irritation causing coughing fits
important_warnings: Do not exceed recommended dose.
May cause mild drowsiness. Avoid alcohol while taking.
contraindications: Patients taking MAO inhibitors within 14 days
Chronic bronchitis or asthma with heavy mucus production
medicines.disclaimer: Consult a doctor if cough lasts more than 7 days or is accompanied by high fever.

medicines.name: Omeprazole / Pantoprazole (Pan 40 / Omez)
common_uses: Relief of frequent heartburn, acid reflux (GERD), and stomach gastritis
Prevention of stomach acid erosion
important_warnings: Take 30 minutes before breakfast with a glass of water.
Not intended for immediate relief of acute heartburn.
medicines.disclaimer: Consult a physician for persistent acid reflux or stomach pain.

medicines.name: Saline Nasal Drops / Spray (Otrivin S / Nasivion Saline)
common_uses: Clearing dry, crusty, or congested nasal passages
Moisturizing nasal membranes to prevent dry nosebleeds
Relief of cold and allergy nasal stuffiness
important_warnings: Safe for daily nasal hygiene when plain saline solution.
Do not share nasal spray bottles to prevent cross-infection.

medicines.name: Loperamide (Imodium)
common_uses: Symptomatic control of sudden acute non-infectious watery diarrhea
Traveler's diarrhea management
important_warnings: Drink plenty of fluids/ORS alongside loperamide.
Do NOT use if high fever or bloody stool is present.
contraindications: Acute ulcerative colitis or bacterial enterocolitis
medicines.disclaimer: Consult a doctor immediately if diarrhea persists longer than 48 hours.
